messages:
Jess - Support: PulsePay hitting 429s from eu-west-1 since ~03:26 UTC. Customer says token-level errors, retries just amplify. They reported ~30% of requests getting 429. Request id sample: req_7f3a2c. :exclamation:
Kai (SRE): grabbing logs now, any sample headers or curl output?
Jess - Support: pasted their curl output below:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-pp-xxxxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1689105960
Retry-After: 5
```
Matt L (Support Lead): 1200/min looks like token RPM cap. PulsePay runs a mix of streaming and polling clients — any sign of minute boundary clustering?
Kai (SRE): yes, metrics show a sawtooth every minute with sharp spikes at :00. Throughput heatmap attached to logs (summary): many short-lived connections opening in same second. Suspect cron/heartbeat alignment + client reconnect strategy.
Emma (Eng): I spun a repro locally: spawn 400 concurrent streaming clients that reconnect every 10s, you see minute-boundary stomping and the token bucket drops Remaining to zero before window reset. Repro script snippet:
```python
# simplified repro idea
for i in range(400):
  spawn(stream_client())
# clients send a 200-400 byte ping every 9s
```
Kai (SRE): quick mitigations: 1) ask customer to add jitter to scheduled jobs/heartbeats, 2) reduce concurrency per API key (pooling), 3) implement exponential backoff + full-jitter on 429s. Also we can issue a temporary quota bump if they need immediate relief.
Jess - Support: I recommended jitter + backoff and requested logs for a replay window. Customer asked for a short-term fix while they change client.
ops-bot: temporary quota increase applied to sk-pp-xxxxx: 1800/min until 2024-11-09T08:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
Matt L (Support Lead): Good. Also advise them to use streaming sessions instead of many short HTTP calls where possible (keeps per-minute count down).
Emma (Eng): long-term: rate limiter is fixed-window per-minute which amplifies aligned bursts. Options: sliding window smoothing or token refill smoothing at the edge. Will open a RFC in eng-runtime with tradeoffs (accuracy vs complexity).
Kai (SRE): created internal ticket #ENGRT-2491 and linked logs + repro. I'll follow up with perf numbers for smoothing.
Jess - Support: Customer accepted temporary quota bump and the jitter/backoff plan. We scheduled a 1:1 with them for 09:00 UTC to validate. :thumbsup:
Matt L (Support Lead): Thanks team. Action items: Jess -> confirm scheduled change, Kai -> attach replay + ticket link, Emma -> RFC draft. Close once customer confirms reduced 429s.
